rows.description: You become the family's strong one for mother or younger siblings. Care for them, but do not deny your own grief. Share responsibilities, let yourself cry, and accept help so strength does not turn into isolation.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, comfort, compassion, grief, guilt, indifference
related mind states: sadness, grief, loneliness

rows.description: After a frightening event such as an accident, assault or violence, the body stays on alert and sleep is disturbed. These are common reactions. Seek trained help, keep routines, and avoid blaming yourself for how you reacted.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, compassion, hope, shame, trust

rows.description: You blame yourself for what happened or for still struggling. It was not your fault, and healing has no deadline. Speak to a counsellor or trusted person; shame grows in silence and fades when shared.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, compassion, fear, hope, trust

rows.description: Relatives say forget it or what will people say. It feels like being silenced. Seek those who believe and support you, share only what you want, and know that being heard is part of recovery.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, compassion, fear, hope, shame

rows.description: A friend confides that they were harmed. Believe them, listen without pressing for details, do not blame, respect their pace, and help them find professional and legal support if they want it. Do not spread their story.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, fear, hope, shame, trust

rows.description: You slowly begin trusting a counsellor with painful memories. Progress is uneven, and it is fine to try another therapist if the fit is poor. Healing is repeated small acts of safety, not a single breakthrough.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, compassion, fear, hope, shame

rows.description: A workplace or college ignored or punished your complaint. It deepens the injury and is not your fault. Keep records, approach internal committees, legal aid or helplines, and lean on people who believe you.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, compassion, fear, hope, shame, trust

rows.description: Anger at those who harmed you or failed to protect you is valid. Use it for boundaries, safety and justice through proper channels. Revenge or bottling it up harms you further, and support can help you channel it.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, compassion, fear, hope, shame, trust

rows.description: Small good days start returning. Let joy in without guilt, and celebrate steps like sleeping better or trusting a friend. Recovery is not forgetting; it is building a life where the past no longer rules.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: anger, betrayal, compassion, fear, shame, trust
related mind states: joy, guilt, hope, trust

rows.description: After hitting early goals, you ask what it was all for. This is a normal question. Explore what you value beyond status: people, craft, service. Small commitments over years give meaning better than one big answer.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, comparison
